checklist_items.19.1: covered: covered here for the container target and on the sibling host case for the host target, which is what this item asks for. On this side the preflight is read and required to report the container capability and runtime for the node, to admit while the node is below its limit, and to answer an administrator-only route as forbidden to a read-only principal with the exact denial code - a denied principal is required to open no socket and to create no audit record or session. A reference that does not exist is required to reach a real failing exit from the PTY with the runtime's own message, to be recorded as an audit entry marked unsuccessful, and to consume no concurrency slot. The platform kill switch is exercised through the settings route: switched off, the preflight must report that it cannot open with the disabled reason and a socket attempt must be refused; switched back on, the preflight must admit again. The host target's preflight and the same kill switch are asserted on the sibling case. This entry is not mutation-proven: the enabled check is made twice - once in the request handler for precedence and message quality and again in the session manager - so removing either one alone leaves the run green, and that redundancy is a product property rather than a gap in the case.
checklist_items.19.2: covered: real target=container WS/PTY, non-echo UTF-8 output and independent exact target file
checklist_items.19.3: covered: covered here for the container target's own pty and on the sibling host case for the frame-split and continuous-output halves of the item. On this side the shell is driven through the real container WS and required to emit multi-byte UTF-8 text that matches exact bytes in the container's own file and in xterm, so the encoding survives the whole path rather than being reassembled loosely. The initial geometry is checked against the browser's own WS rows and cols and against the pty's reported size, and a viewport change is then required to make the browser send a resize frame carrying different, valid geometry and to make the container's shell report that same size afterwards - a UI that resized only its canvas, or a frame the server dropped, leaves the pty at the old geometry and fails here. Arbitrary frame splitting and a burst of consecutive lines are asserted on the host case with a byte gate, where the agent path can be held deterministically. Proven by mutation: dropping the resize call that follows the refit fails with the browser never reporting its new geometry.
checklist_items.19.4: covered: four distinct endings are exercised on the same real container WS. A shell exit is required to deliver a successful exit frame carrying code zero, to show the ended state, and to be audited as a shell exit. A tab close is required to be audited as a client close. A context that goes away is required to end the same way. A real network break is then forced by taking the browser offline, so the socket dies without a close handshake and the page cannot tidy up after itself - the server is still required to end the session, and in every one of the four cases the shell's own PID and start time, read independently from the container, are required to be gone and the node's active count is required to return to zero, so a leaked pty or a leaked concurrency slot fails here rather than being invisible. Recovery after a disconnect is not applicable to this product: the server reports a node or shell disconnect as the end of the session and offers no reattach, which is why the four cases above all assert termination and release rather than a resume - there is no resume to resume.
checklist_items.19.5: covered: The admission limit is real and the release is real. Sessions are opened on one node until the server itself reports the node full, each one gated on the server having counted the previous one rather than on the page having rendered. At that point the preflight is required to answer that it cannot open, with a non-empty reason and an active count at or above the limit. A further socket is then opened directly from a signed-in page and required to be refused, so the case fails on the server's admission answer rather than on a rendering detail, and the refused attempt is required not to have pushed the active count past the limit. Closing every held terminal is required to return the node to an empty state that accepts a session again, so a leaked slot would fail here. The idle policy is required to be a positive number of minutes as reported by the server, because a zero would silently mean never and the notice it drives would be unreachable. Proven by mutation: moving the per-node comparison from at-the-limit to past-the-limit makes the extra socket connect and the case fails with a full node accepting another terminal socket.
checklist_items.19.6: covered: audit admin principal/node/container ref and close result; no credentials or arbitrary terminal content exported

checklist_items.12.1-12.8: N/A: this surface is a full page, not a business dialog. The terminal page and the terminal component it mounts render no modal, drawer, popover or dropdown at all - there is no component to open from an entry point, no first step to verify, no footer action area to keep clear of the content, and no delete preview, revision or compare-and-swap to inspect. The dialog contracts this section describes are exercised on the surfaces that do own them, and nothing is invented here for a page that has none of those parts.
checklist_items.13.1-13.6: N/A: this surface has no floating control to drive. There is no trigger button, menu, dropdown, tooltip or notification anywhere on the terminal page or in the terminal component, so there is no accessible name to check on a trigger, no list of menu items whose permissions could be compared with the API, no overlay whose placement at the viewport edge could be measured, no tooltip standing in for an action, and no notification to reconcile with a stored result or to check for repeats. The entry point that does exist is covered on the page that owns it, and no such control is invented here.
